primary_claim: A single-layer transformer with two sequential (recurrent) applications of the same attention head can form induction heads, and even a model with the OV circuit removed entirely still shows an induction-like bump, suggesting induction depends on composition of attention-head applications rather than strictly on separate layers or an explicit OV circuit.

effect.metric: validation perplexity / induction bump / copy accuracy, baseline vs No-OV transformer
effect.value: perplexity 24.65 (baseline) vs 26.73 (No-OV); induction bump 2.816 vs 2.715; copy accuracy 0.195 vs 0.556

contradicts_or_qualifies: Anthropic's stated claim that induction heads don't occur in 1-layer models because they require a composition of attention heads in different layers
stated_future_work: explore further whether transformers can run without explicit OV circuits if the pattern continues to hold at larger scale
quote: This lead me to hypothesise if removing OV circuit in The Transformer allows it to function and still form Induction heads . Turns out it does
